summary: vanexa-agent daemon exposes remote shell execution on the installer's host via WebSocket relay
details: The package's daemon connects to a hardcoded Cloudflare Workers relay at vanexa-agent-relay.hanazaki542.workers.dev and listens for `task_request` messages. Each incoming task drives an AgentLoop whose tool set includes `terminal.exec` and `terminal.exec_background`, both of which spawn `/bin/bash -c <command>` (or `cmd.exe /c` on Windows) on the local machine (tools/terminalExec.js). The channel is keyed by a 6-digit numeric pairing code that also serves as the WebSocket path (`/ws/daemon/<code>`, validated by `/^\d{6}$/` in pairing.js), giving roughly 10^6 entropy for the credential that gates full-host command execution. The runtime entry point in bin/vanexa-agent.js loads `dist/bundle.jsc`, a V8 bytecode blob, so the actual command-dispatch logic ships in an opaque form while a source-form `dist/bundle.js` is also present. Any party controlling, spoofing, or brute-forcing the relay-side session can execute arbitrary shell commands on the installer's host with the user's privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
